children.story_en: Rama and his brothers remember their father and perform a respectful water rite together.
children.story_ta: Rama and his brothers remember their father and perform a respectful water rite together.
children.learning_objective: Families may show care for the departed through remembrance and respectful duty.

children.story_en: Rama greets the mothers with respect, and the family shares sorrow without giving up kindness.
children.story_ta: Rama greets the mothers with respect, and the family shares sorrow without giving up kindness.
children.learning_objective: Respectful greeting and compassion can help a family face grief together.

children.story_en: Bharata asks Rama to return, but Rama explains that he must keep the promise made to their father.
children.story_ta: Bharata asks Rama to return, but Rama explains that he must keep the promise made to their father.
children.learning_objective: Keeping a difficult promise is presented as a serious responsibility in the source narrative.

children.story_en: Rama reminds Bharata that life changes and encourages him to act with steadiness and duty.
children.story_ta: Rama reminds Bharata that life changes and encourages him to act with steadiness and duty.
children.learning_objective: The source presents steadiness and duty as responses to grief; this is an educational reflection, not a promise of an outcome.

children.story_en: Bharata asks Rama to come home and rule, while Rama remains committed to his forest duty.
children.story_ta: Bharata asks Rama to come home and rule, while Rama remains committed to his forest duty.
children.learning_objective: The brothers disagree about the right course but continue to speak within a bond of respect.

children.story_en: Rama and Bharata agree to carry out different duties while caring for their people and family.
children.story_ta: Rama and Bharata agree to carry out different duties while caring for their people and family.
children.learning_objective: Shared responsibility can mean taking different roles for a common purpose.

children.story_en: Jabali gives Rama one way of thinking about the decision; Rama will answer with his own view of truth and duty.
children.story_ta: Jabali gives Rama one way of thinking about the decision; Rama will answer with his own view of truth and duty.
children.learning_objective: A respectful classroom discussion can compare different arguments without treating every argument as settled truth.

children.story_en: Rama explains why truth and responsibility matter to him, even when another person offers a different argument.
children.story_ta: Rama explains why truth and responsibility matter to him, even when another person offers a different argument.
children.learning_objective: The source presents truthfulness and responsibility as values Rama chooses to uphold.

children.story_en: Vasistha tells Rama about the royal family line and asks him to care for the people as king.
children.story_ta: Vasistha tells Rama about the royal family line and asks him to care for the people as king.
children.learning_objective: The source connects leadership with family duty and care for the people.

children.story_en: Vasistha explains that families and teachers deserve respect; Rama and Bharata each try to carry out their responsibilities.
children.story_ta: Vasistha explains that families and teachers deserve respect; Rama and Bharata each try to carry out their responsibilities.
children.learning_objective: Respect for parents and teachers is presented as a duty, while the brothers continue to act with care.

children.story_en: Rama gives his sandals to Bharata, who will use them as a reminder of Rama while caring for Ayodhya.
children.story_ta: Rama gives his sandals to Bharata, who will use them as a reminder of Rama while caring for Ayodhya.
children.learning_objective: A symbol can represent trust and responsibility when people must serve in different places.

children.story_en: Bharata respectfully carries Rama’s sandals home and returns to care for the kingdom.
children.story_ta: Bharata respectfully carries Rama’s sandals home and returns to care for the kingdom.
children.learning_objective: The return journey is framed by respect, responsibility, and care for the people.
